title: MATH GAOKAO - 407
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Use similar triangles to determine an unknown height from shadow lengths.
questions.question: A vertical pole \(2\) meters tall casts a shadow \(3\) meters long. At the same time, a nearby tree casts a shadow \(12\) meters long. Assuming the sun's rays are parallel, how tall is the tree? Both objects are vertical and stand on the same level ground.
questions.explanation:
The pole and its shadow form a right triangle similar to the tree and its shadow. Thus
\[
\frac{\text{pole height}}{\text{pole shadow}}=\frac{\text{tree height}}{\text{tree shadow}}.
\]
So \(\frac{2}{3}=\frac{h}{12}\). Multiplying by \(12\) gives \(h=8\). The tree is \(8\) meters tall.
questions.hint: Set up a proportion between height and shadow length for similar right triangles.

questions.learningObjective: Model the area of a circular path as the difference between two circle areas.
questions.question: A circular flower bed has radius \(5\) meters. A uniform path \(2\) meters wide surrounds it. What is the area of the path?
questions.explanation:
The outer radius is \(5+2=7\) meters. The path area is the difference between the outer and inner circle areas:
\[
\pi(7^2)-\pi(5^2)=\pi(49-25)=24\pi.
\]
So the path area is \(24\pi\) square meters.
questions.hint: Find the outer radius, then subtract the area of the inner circle from the area of the outer circle.

questions.concept: Pythagorean Theorem in a Ladder Model
questions.learningObjective: Apply the Pythagorean theorem to find a missing length in a right-triangle model.
questions.question: A \(13\)-meter ladder leans against a vertical wall. Its base is \(5\) meters from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation:
The wall, ground, and ladder form a right triangle with ladder as hypotenuse. By the Pythagorean theorem,
\[
h^2+5^2=13^2.
\]
Thus \(h^2=169-25=144\), so \(h=12\). The ladder reaches \(12\) meters up the wall.
questions.hint: Treat the ladder as the hypotenuse of a right triangle and use \(a^2+b^2=c^2\).

questions.learningObjective: Model the capacity of a cylindrical tank using the volume formula for a cylinder.
questions.question: A cylindrical water tank has radius \(3\) meters and height \(5\) meters. What is its volume?
questions.explanation:
The volume of a cylinder is \(V=\pi r^2h\). Substituting \(r=3\) and \(h=5\),
\[
V=\pi(3^2)(5)=45\pi.
\]
So the volume is \(45\pi\) cubic meters.
questions.hint: Use the cylinder volume formula \(V=\pi r^2h\).

questions.learningObjective: Use a scale factor to convert map dimensions to actual area.
questions.question: On a map with scale \(1:200\), a rectangular plot measures \(3\text{ cm}\) by \(4\text{ cm}\). What is the actual area of the plot?
questions.explanation:
The actual dimensions are \(3\cdot 200=600\text{ cm}\) \(=6\text{ m}\) and \(4\cdot 200=800\text{ cm}\) \(=8\text{ m}\). Therefore the actual area is
\[
6\cdot 8=48
\]
square meters.
questions.hint: Convert each map length to its actual length using the scale, then multiply the actual side lengths.

questions.learningObjective: Model distance traveled by a rolling wheel using circumference.
questions.question: A wheel has radius \(0.5\) meters and rolls without slipping along a straight path. How far does it travel in \(100\) complete revolutions?
questions.explanation:
One revolution covers the circumference \[
\begin{aligned}
C&=2\pi r \\
&=2\pi(0.5) \\
&=\pi
\end{aligned}
\] meters. In \(100\) revolutions, the distance is
\[
100\pi
\]
meters.
questions.hint: First find the circumference of the wheel, then multiply by the number of revolutions.

questions.learningObjective: Use the cube of a linear scale factor to compare volumes of similar containers.
questions.question: Two similar cylindrical containers have heights in the ratio \(2:3\). If the smaller container holds \(40\) liters, how many liters does the larger container hold?
questions.explanation:
For similar solids, volumes scale as the cube of the linear scale factor. The linear ratio is \(\frac{3}{2}\), so the volume ratio is
\[
\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3=\frac{27}{8}.
\]
Thus the larger volume is
\[
40\cdot\frac{27}{8}=135
\]
liters.
questions.hint: Use the fact that volume ratios for similar solids equal the cube of the corresponding length ratio.

questions.learningObjective: Determine an angle of elevation from a right-triangle model.
questions.question: A vertical tower \(20\) meters tall casts a horizontal shadow \(20\sqrt{3}\) meters long. What is the angle of elevation of the sun?
questions.explanation:
In the right triangle formed by the tower, its shadow, and a sun ray,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tan\theta&=\frac{\text{tower height}}{\text{shadow length}} \\
&=\frac{20}{20\sqrt{3}} \\
&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\tan 30^\circ=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), the angle of elevation is \(30^\circ\).
questions.hint: Use \(\tan\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}\) with the tower as the opposite side.

questions.learningObjective: Model a fencing problem and find the maximum rectangular area.
questions.question: A farmer has \(120\) meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular pen along a straight river. No fence is needed along the river. What is the maximum possible area of the pen?
questions.explanation:
Let \(x\) be the length perpendicular to the river and \(y\) the length parallel to the river. The fencing is used on two sides of length \(x\) and one side of length \(y\), so
\[
2x+y=120,\quad y=120-2x.
\]
The area is
\[
A=x(120-2x)=120x-2x^2.
\]
This quadratic has maximum at \(x=\frac{120}{2\cdot 2}=30\). Then \(y=120-60=60\), and
\[
A_{\max}=30\cdot 60=1800.
\]
So the maximum area is \(1800\) square meters.
questions.hint: Let the side perpendicular to the river be \(x\), write the parallel side in terms of \(x\), then maximize the resulting quadratic area.

questions.learningObjective: Model and minimize the surface area of an open-top box with fixed volume.
questions.question: An open-top rectangular box has a square base of side \(x\) meters and height \(h\) meters. Its volume is \(32\) cubic meters. What is the minimum possible surface area of the box?
questions.explanation:
Since the dimensions are positive, \(x>0\) and \(h>0\). The volume condition gives
\[
x^2h=32,\qquad h=\frac{32}{x^2}.
\]
The surface area consists of the square base and four side rectangles:
\[
S(x)=x^2+4xh=x^2+\frac{128}{x}.
\]
Differentiate and solve for a stationary point:
\[
\begin{aligned}
S'(x)&=2x-\frac{128}{x^2},\\
2x&=\frac{128}{x^2},\\
2x^3&=128,\\
x^3&=64,\\
x&=4.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(x>0\), the sign of \(S'(x)\) is the sign of \(2(x^3-64)\). Hence \(S\) decreases on \((0,4)\) and increases on \((4,\infty)\), so \(x=4\) gives the global minimum. Its value is
\[
S(4)=16+\frac{128}{4}=48.
\]
The minimum surface area is \(48\) square meters, attained when \(x=4\) meters and \(h=2\) meters.
questions.hint: Express the height in terms of \(x\) using the volume, write the surface area as a function of \(x\), and minimize it.
